Rashi on Eruvin 47a:10:1.hebrew: למה ליה - למיפסק הלכה כרבי יהודה, דר' מאיר פליג עליה? הא כיילת לעיל: להיכא דלא איתמר הלכה לא כמר ולא כמר — עבדינן כרבי יהודה:
Rashi on Eruvin 47a:10:1.english: Why did he [need to] - To rule the halakha in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, where Rabbi Meir disputes him? Behold, you established a general rule above: wherever the halakha was not stated — neither like this master nor like that master — we act in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda!

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:11:1.hebrew: רב לית ליה להני כללי - ומשום דרב לית ליה קאמרת ליתנהו? והא ר' יוחנן קאמר להו, והלכה כר' יוחנן:
Rashi on Eruvin 47a:11:1.english: Rav does not accept these principles - And because Rav does not accept them, do you say that they do not exist? But behold, Rabbi Yochanan stated them, and the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yochanan!

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:12:1.hebrew: היבמה לא תחלוץ - בתוך ג' חדשים למיתת בעלה. מפרש טעמא ביבמות: שמא מעוברת היא, וחליצת מעוברת אינה חליצה. וא"ת: תחלוץ בתוך ג' ותמתין עד לאחר ג' — שאם תמצא מעוברת, אינה צריכה חליצה אם תלד וולד של קיימא; ואם לא תמצא מעוברת, אינה צריכה חליצה אחרת; ואם תלד וולד שאינו של קיימא, תחלוץ פעם שניה? שמא יהא וולד של קיימא, ואינה חליצה לאוסרה לכהונה, ונמצא מצריכה כרוז לכהונה. וליצרכה? דלמא איכא דהוי בחליצה ולא הוי בהכרזה, וסבר: שרו חלוצה לכהן:
Rashi on Eruvin 47a:12:1.english: The yevama may not perform ḥalitza - Within three months of her husband’s death. The reason is explained in [tractate] Yevamot: perhaps she is pregnant, and the ḥalitza of a pregnant woman is not [valid] ḥalitza. And if you say: Let her perform ḥalitza within three [months] and wait until after three [months], for if she is found to be pregnant, she will not need ḥalitza if she gives birth to a viable child; and if she is not found to be pregnant, she will not need another ḥalitza; and if she gives birth to a child that is not viable, let her perform ḥalitza a second time? [The answer is:] Perhaps the child will be viable, and it is not [a valid] ḥalitza to disqualify her from the priesthood, and [the court] would consequently need to issue a proclamation [permitting her] to the priesthood. And let [the court] require it? Perhaps there will be someone who was present at the ḥalitza and was not present at the proclamation, and he will think: They have permitted a ḥalutza to [marry] a priest.

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:12:2.hebrew: ולא תתייבם - שמא מעוברת היא, ונמצא בא על אשת אחיו שיש לה בנים, והרי היא עליו בכרת. אבל לאחר שלשה — דניכר בה שאינה מעוברת — או תחלוץ או תתייבם:
Rashi on Eruvin 47a:12:2.english: Nor undergo levirate marriage - Lest she is pregnant, and he will turn out to have engaged in relations with his brother’s wife who has children, and behold, she is [forbidden] to him under penalty of excision [karet]. But after three [months] — when it is discernible in her that she is not pregnant — she may either perform ḥalitza or undergo levirate marriage.

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:13:1.hebrew: שאר כל הנשים כו' - שמא תלד בתוך תשעה למיתת בעלה, ספק בן שבעה לאחרון, ספק בן תשעה לראשון. ובעינן הבחנה, כדאמרינן ביבמות (דף מב.): שמא ייבם אשת אחיו מאמו, ועוד יש איסורין הרבה:
Rashi on Eruvin 47a:13:1.english: All other women, etc. - Lest she give birth within nine [months] of her [first] husband's death, [and there will be an] uncertainty [whether the child is] a seven-month [child] of the latter [husband] or a nine-month [child] of the former [husband]. And we require discernment [of paternity], as we say in Yevamot (42a): Lest [one] perform levirate marriage with the wife of his maternal brother, and furthermore there are many [other] prohibitions.

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:13:2.english: Nor be betrothed - The Rabbis decreed [against] betrothal on account of marriage.

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:13:3.hebrew: אחת בתולות כו' - מפרש התם (שם:): אחת שנישאו לזה כשהן בתולות, ואחת שנישאו לזה כשהן בעולות — שנתאלמנה או נתגרשה מבעלה זה, בין מן האירוסין בין מן הנשואין — צריכות להמתין אחר הגט או אחר המיתה ג' חדשים:
Rashi on Eruvin 47a:13:3.english: Whether virgins, etc. - [The Gemara] explains there (ibid.): Both those who were married to this [man] when they were virgins and those who were married to this [man] when they were non-virgins — whether she was widowed or divorced from this husband of hers, whether from betrothal or from marriage — must wait three months after the bill of divorce or after the death.

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:13:4.hebrew: אחת ארוסות - אף על גב דארוסה לא בת עיבורי היא, גזור רבנן ארוסה אטו נשואה. דברי ר"מ לא גרסי', אלא סתמא היא:
Rashi on Eruvin 47a:13:4.english: Whether betrothed [women] - Even though a betrothed woman is not subject to pregnancy, the Sages decreed [a waiting period for] a betrothed woman on account of a married woman. We do not read: "The statement of Rabbi Meir"; rather, it is an anonymous [mishna].

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:14:1.hebrew: יתארסו - מיד, דהא לא מיעברא משני תוך ג'. ואם תלד בתוך ט' — ודאי דראשון הוא, דאי מאחרון, בן ששה הוא ולא חיי:
Rashi on Eruvin 47a:14:1.english: May be betrothed - Immediately, as she will not become pregnant from the second [husband] within three [months]. And if she gives birth within nine [months], [the child] is certainly the first [husband's], for if [conceived] from the latter [husband], it is [a child born at] six months and does not survive.

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:15:1.hebrew: והארוסות - שנתאלמנו או שנתגרשו מן האירוסין, ינשאו מיד, דהא לא מיעברא מראשון:
Rashi on Eruvin 47a:15:1.english: And betrothed women - [Those] who were widowed or divorced from betrothal may be married immediately, as [such a woman] is not pregnant from the first [husband].

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:15:2.hebrew: חוץ מן הארוסה שביהודה - שהיו רגילין ליחד חתן וכלה קודם כניסתן לחופה, כדאמרינן בכתובות (דף יב.):
Rashi on Eruvin 47a:15:2.english: Except for a betrothed woman in Judea - For they were accustomed to seclude [the] bridegroom and bride before their entry into the wedding canopy, as we say in Ketubot (12a).

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:15:3.english: [His heart] is bold with her - [He is] accustomed to her and familiar with her, and she is agreeable to him.

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:16:1.hebrew: כל הנשים יתארסו - אתנא קמא פליג דאסר אפי' ליארס, ואדרבי יהודה פליג דשרי ארוסה לינשא:
Rashi on Eruvin 47a:16:1.english: All the women may be betrothed - He disagrees with the First Tanna, who prohibited even being betrothed, and he disagrees with Rabbi Yehuda, who permitted a betrothed woman to marry.

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:16:2.hebrew: חוץ מן האלמנה מפני האיבול - שאסורה ליארס כל ימי אבלה, אבל גרושה תיארס מיד:
Rashi on Eruvin 47a:16:2.english: Except for a widow, because of the mourning - For she is forbidden to be betrothed throughout the days of her mourning, but a divorcee may be betrothed immediately.

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:17:1.english: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei - Who permits [women] to be betrothed immediately.

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:17:2.hebrew: ואמרינן - מכלל דהך סתמא דתניא לעיל, "אחת ארוסות ואחת נשואות", יחידאה היא:
Rashi on Eruvin 47a:17:2.english: And we said - [Does it follow] by inference that this anonymous [ruling] that was taught above, "whether betrothed or married," is [the opinion of] a single individual?

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:18:1.english: And was it not taught - [This is stated] in an affirmative tone.

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:18:2.hebrew: רדופה לילך לבית אביה - תדירה לדור בבית אביה בעיר אחרת, ואינה רגילה עם בעלה:
Rashi on Eruvin 47a:18:2.english: Eager to go to her father’s house - [She was] accustomed to live in her father’s house in another city, and was not regularly with her husband.

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:18:3.english: Sick - And she cannot endure the exertion of marital relations.

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:18:4.hebrew: עקרה - מחמת מזל, שכבר נישאת לג' בני אדם ולא ילדה להן, והוחזקה עקרה:
Rashi on Eruvin 47a:18:4.english: Barren - Due to [her] constellation, as she had already been married to three men and did not bear children to them, and was established as a barren woman.

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:18:5.hebrew: איילונית - ממעי אמה, ויש לה סימנין: שאין לה שערות ולא דדין. ולשון איילונית — דוכרניתא, כאיל זה שאינו יולד:
Rashi on Eruvin 47a:18:5.english: A sexually underdeveloped woman [ayalonit] - [She is barren] from her mother’s womb, and she has signs: that she has no [pubic] hair and no breasts. And the term ayalonit [means] dokhranita [a male-like female], like this ram [ayil], which does not give birth.

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:18:6.english: And [a woman] who is unfit to give birth - Due to [drinking] a potion of drugs.

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:18:7.hebrew: דברי ר"מ - אלמא ר"מ הוא דגזר בההיא דפשיטא לן דאינה מעוברת, וה"ה לארוסה:
Rashi on Eruvin 47a:18:7.english: The words of Rabbi Meir - It follows that it is Rabbi Meir who decreed in that [case] where it is obvious to us that she is not pregnant, and the same applies to a betrothed woman.

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:19:1.hebrew: ולמה ליה - לר' יוחנן למימר הלכה כר' יוסי, דהא איהו גופיה כייל לעיל: ר"מ ורבי יוסי הלכה כר' יוסי? אלא, ש"מ לא אמר ר' יוחנן להני כללי, אלא הנך אמוראי אמרינהו מנפשייהו:
Rashi on Eruvin 47a:19:1.english: And why did he need [it] - For Rabbi Yoḥanan to say that the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, since he himself formulated as a rule earlier: "[Between] Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yosei, the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei"? Rather, conclude from this: Rabbi Yoḥanan did not state these general rules; rather, those Amoraim stated them on their own.

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:1:1.hebrew: שלש חצירות - לקמן בכיצד מעברין (עירובין דף נט.), וקאמר ר' יהודה: עיר של רבים ונעשית של יחיד — שנתמעטו אוכלוסיה מעבור ברחובותיה ששים ריבוא, ולא דמיא השתא לדגלי מדבר — אין מערבין את כולה יחד, אלא אם שייר חוצה לה נ' דיורין שלא יערבו עמה, למיהוי היכר לעיר של רבים, דלא ליערבו כולה אלא מבואות מבואות. ר"ש אומר: דיו לשייר ג' חצירות של ב' ב' בעלי בתים:
Rashi on Eruvin 47a:1:1.english: Three courtyards - [This is taught] below in [the chapter entitled] Keitzad Me'abrin (Eruvin 59a), and Rabbi Yehuda says: [In the case of] a public city that became a private [city] — in that its population decreased from six hundred thousand passing through its streets, and it is no longer similar to the banners of the wilderness — they may not establish an eiruv for all of it together, unless one left outside of it fifty dwellings that do not join in the eiruv with it, in order to serve as a reminder that [it was formerly] a public city, so that they should not establish an eiruv for all of it [together], but rather alleyway by alleyway. Rabbi Shimon says: It is sufficient to leave [outside] three courtyards of two homeowners each.

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:20:1.hebrew: ומאי קושיא דלמא - אע"ג דכיילינהו ר' יוחנן, איצטריך ליה למיפסק בהא משום דהוה רבי מאיר מחמיר, ואמר שמואל: הלכה כרבי מאיר בגזירותיו בכל מקום שהחמיר. ואתא רבי יוחנן לאפוקי לדשמואל, מיהא דבהא הלכה כרבי יוסי:
Rashi on Eruvin 47a:20:1.english: And what is the difficulty? Perhaps - Even though Rabbi Yoḥanan formulated [these] general rules, it was necessary for him to rule [specifically] in this [case], because Rabbi Meir was stringent and Shmuel said: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Meir in his decrees, wherever he was stringent. And Rabbi Yoḥanan came to exclude [the statement] of Shmuel, at least [to make clear] that in this [case] the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei.

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:21:1.hebrew: ליריד - שוק הנקבע ליום חג של גוים. ולוקחין מהן בתים ושדות — מפני שממעיטן, אי נמי משום ישוב א"י:
Rashi on Eruvin 47a:21:1.english: To a fair - A market established for a festival day of gentiles. And “one may buy houses and fields from them” [is permitted] because he diminishes them, or alternatively, because of settling the Land of Israel.

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:21:2.english: Animals, and slaves, and maidservants - Because he brings them into sanctity.

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:21:4.hebrew: בערכאות שלהן - לפני דייניהן לחתום. ואע"פ שהוא חשיבות להן, ואיכא למיחש דלמא אזלי ומודו — אפ"ה שרי:
Rashi on Eruvin 47a:21:4.english: In their courts - Before their judges, to sign [the deed]. And even though this accords them importance, and there is [reason] to be concerned lest they go and give thanks [to their idols] — even so, it is permitted.

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:21:5.english: Because he is like one who rescues from their hands - So that the gentile will not retract and contest the sale.

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:23:1.hebrew: בית הקברות ס"ד - הא עבר בלאו:
Rashi on Eruvin 47a:23:1.english: A cemetery, can it enter your mind? - Behold, he violates a negative commandment.

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:25:1.english: When he cannot find [a place] to study - In his [own] land.

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:3:1.hebrew: אוסר על בני חצירות - שלא יוציאו מבתיהן לחצר, מפני שיש לו רשות בחצר. ואע"פ שאינו בעיר, אוסר עליהן אם לא עירב קודם שהלך:
Rashi on Eruvin 47a:3:1.english: Prohibits the residents of the courtyards - That they may not carry out from their houses into the courtyard, because he has rights in the courtyard; and even though he is not in the town, he prohibits them if he did not make an eiruv before he left.

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:4:1.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: He does not prohibit - Since he is not in the city.

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:4:2.hebrew: נכרי אוסר - אף על פי שאינו בעיר, שהרי יכול לבא, ואין זה היסח מן הלב. אבל ישראל, משהלך מכאן ולא בא מערב שבת, הסיח לביתו מלבו כל השבת, שהרי לא יבא; הלכך, כמאן דלית ליה להך דירה בעלים דמי:
Rashi on Eruvin 47a:4:2.english: A gentile prohibits - Even though he is not in the town, as he is able to come, and this is not a dismissal from the heart. But a Jew, once he has gone from here and has not arrived before Shabbat, has dismissed his house from his heart for the entire Shabbat, as he will not come; therefore, it is considered as if this dwelling has no owner.

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:4:3.hebrew: לשבות אצל בתו - מאמש, אפילו באותה העיר:
Rashi on Eruvin 47a:4:3.english: To spend Shabbat with his daughter - [He went] from yesterday evening, even in the same town:

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:5:1.hebrew: רבי יהודה פליג עליה - דאמר: בעיר אחרת אינו אוסר, הא באותה העיר אוסר. ורבי יוסי נמי פליג עליה, אלא חד מינייהו נקט:
Rashi on Eruvin 47a:5:1.english: Rabbi Yehuda disagrees with him - For he said [that] in a different town he does not prohibit, which implies that in that same town he does prohibit. And Rabbi Yosei also disagrees with him, but [the Gemara] merely cited one of them.

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:7:1.english: That is what they said - It is [a Mishnah] in our chapter (daf 49b).

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:7:2.hebrew: אנו אין לנו - שיכול לקנות שביתה ברגליו בלא עירוב פת, אלא עני — כלומר, מי שהוא בדרך ואין עמו פת:
Rashi on Eruvin 47a:7:2.english: We have no [one] - Who can acquire [Shabbat] residence with his feet without an eiruv of bread, except for a pauper — that is to say, one who is on the road and has no bread with him.

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:8:1.hebrew: אחד עשיר - היושב בביתו, אם רצה לילך בעצמו ולהחשיך שם על התחום — קונה לו שביתה:
Rashi on Eruvin 47a:8:1.english: A wealthy person alike - [Even one] who sits in his house, if he wishes to go himself and wait until nightfall there at the [Shabbat] boundary, he acquires a [Shabbat] residence.

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:8:2.hebrew: שלא יצא - מפני הטורח, ויערב ברגליו, אלא התירו לשלוח עירוב בפת ע"י שלוחו:
Rashi on Eruvin 47a:8:2.english: So that he not go out - [This is] on account of the exertion, [so that he does not have to go out] and establish an eiruv with his feet; rather, they permitted sending an eiruv with bread via his agent.

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:9:1.hebrew: ומתני ליה רב חייא בר אשי - למתני' לחייא בר רב קמיה דרב:
Rashi on Eruvin 47a:9:1.english: And Rav Ḥiyya bar Ashi taught him - [He was teaching] the Mishnah to Ḥiyya bar Rav in the presence of Rav.

Rashi on Eruvin 47a:9:2.english: Both a pauper and a wealthy person - [He was teaching] the statement of Rabbi Yehuda.

Tosafot on Eruvin 47a:19:1.english: This is our reading: "Rabbi Yosei permits [her] to be betrothed and to marry immediately" - And there is no need to elaborate here.
